The intrinsic precision of 2D/2D rigid image registration is limited to 0.5 mm and 0.5°, whereas the intrinsic precision of a 3D/2D registration is limited to the intrinsic precision of the 2D/3D registration, plus the 2D image registration.

1) 3D/ 3D rigid registration of CBCT images is a reliable method for patient setup in radiotherapy; 2) the precision of 3-D/3-D rigid registration of CB-CBCT images is 0.5 to 0.8 mm; and 3) the precision of the method is independent of the number of image slices and the number of points used in the registration.
the intrinsic precision of the 3D/ 3D rigid image registrations of patient CT and CBCT images is 1 mm for the translational parameters and 1 degree for the rotational parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of 3D rigid image alignment in the absence of ground truth.
the problem of 3D rigid registration of images in the presence of a large number of outliers.
assessing the intrinsic precision of the rigid registration process, i.e. the ability of the algorithm to accurately estimate the rigid body motion between the two image sets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3D-3D registration of the two datasets is a very difficult task and that the results are not very reliable.
there is no single optimal registration algorithm.
the 3D/ 3D rigid image-registration method is not sufficiently precise to be used as a patient setup tool for the treatment of prostate cancer in the absence of ground truth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the precision of rigid registration is limited by the precision with which the patient is set up on the treatment machine.
we have developed a method for assessing the intrinsic precision of rigid image registration results in the absence of the ground truth.
we have developed an efficient method for 3D/ 3D rigid image-registration in the presence of intensity inhomogeneity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intrinsic precision of rigid image registration can be assessed in the absence of an absolute ground truth.
the use of a 4D CT in a deformable image registration (DIR) workflow can improve the accuracy and precision of the DIR results, especially in regions of the lung with high deformation.
, when assessing the precision of 3d/3d rigid registration results, the choice of the ground truth can be crucial.
